description: OpenDER is EPRI's Python model of photovoltaic and battery-storage inverter behaviour for distribution-network studies. It represents steady-state and dynamic responses associated with IEEE 1547-2018 capabilities, informed by observed commercial equipment. Inputs include grid conditions and configured resource settings; outputs include power and trip or service-entry behaviour. Spatial coverage is an individual distributed resource coupled to a chosen network, and temporal resolution follows the snapshot, quasi-static time-series or dynamic experiment. Free BSD-3-Clause source includes installation instructions and notebooks. The example alternates grid voltage over roughly ten-minute intervals to demonstrate tripping and reconnection. A limitation is that represented interconnection functions and parameter choices must match the equipment being studied; software reuse does not certify a particular inverter. OpenDER supports distribution planning and resilience simulations. A separately linked interface connects it with OpenDSS (platform-opendss). No circuit or model was executed.
inputs: Grid voltage and other operating conditions
